::: {#exr-reuse-features}

#### Reusing the convolutional layers

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
is_low = y_train < 5
n_low = int(is_low.sum())
low_net = train(make_cnn(n_classes=5), x_train[is_low], y_train[is_low])
low_test = y_test < 5
low_acc = accuracy(low_net, x_test[low_test], y_test[low_test])


def new_head(train_all, seed=3):
    # Copy low_net with a new last layer; return it and the parameters to train.
    net = copy.deepcopy(low_net)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    net[-1] = nn.Linear(16 * 4 * 4, 5)
    if train_all:
        return net, net.parameters()
    return net, net[-1].parameters()


print(n_low, low_acc)
```

The [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set) has `r py$n_low` labelled images of the digits 0 to 4.
`low_net` is `make_cnn(n_classes=5)` trained on them.
`new_head()` copies `low_net`,
replaces its last linear layer with a new one for the digits 5 to 9,
and returns the copy with the [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter) to train.
With `train_all=False`,
those are only the new layer's.
The [convolutional layers](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-convolutional-layer) keep the weights they learned on the digits 0 to 4.
Trained this way on the 20 images of each draw,
is the network more accurate than the networks of @sol-few-labels?

:::
